verses.text: In those days, Caesar Augustus issued an order: everybody across the empire had to get registered.
This was the first registration, while Quirinius was governing Syria.
Everyone went to register, each person heading to their own town.
Joseph went too, traveling up from Nazareth in Galilee to Judea, to David’s town, Bethlehem. He belonged to David’s family line,
and went to register with Mary, who was engaged to him and was pregnant.
While they were there, the time came for Mary to give birth.
She gave birth to her firstborn son, wrapped him in cloths, and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no space for them in the guest room. 👶
Nearby, shepherds were staying out in the fields, keeping watch over their flock at night.
Suddenly, an angel of the Lord stood near them, and the Lord’s glory shone all around. They were terrified.
The angel said, “Don’t be afraid! Look, I’m bringing you good news that will make everyone very happy.”
“Today, in David’s town, a Savior has been born for you. He is Christ the Lord.”
“Here’s your sign: you’ll find a baby wrapped in cloths and lying in a feeding trough.”
All at once, a huge heavenly army appeared with the angel, praising God and saying:
“Glory to God in the highest heaven, and peace on earth to the people he favors!” 🌟
When the angels went back into heaven, the shepherds said to each other, “Let’s go straight to Bethlehem and see what happened—the Lord has let us know about it.”
They hurried there and found Mary, Joseph, and the baby lying in the feeding trough.
After seeing him, they spread the word about what they’d been told about this child.
Everyone who heard the shepherds’ story was amazed at what they said.
Mary held onto all these words and kept turning them over in her heart.
The shepherds went back, praising and glorifying God for everything they’d heard and seen. It all happened just as they’d been told. 🙌
When the baby was eight days old and it was time to circumcise him, they named him Jesus—the name the angel had given before he was conceived.
When the time came for their purification under Moses’ Law, they brought Jesus to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord,
as the Lord’s Law says: “Every firstborn boy must be called holy to the Lord.”
They also came to offer the sacrifice required by the Lord’s Law: “a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.”
There was a man in Jerusalem named Simeon. He was righteous and devoted, waiting for Israel’s consolation, and the Holy Spirit was with him.
The Holy Spirit had revealed to him that he wouldn’t die before seeing the Lord’s Christ.
Guided by the Spirit, Simeon came into the temple. When Jesus’ parents brought the child in to do what the Law required,
Simeon took Jesus in his arms and praised God, saying:
“Master, now you can let your servant go in peace, just as you promised.”
“My eyes have seen your salvation,”
“which you prepared for all peoples to see—”
“a light to reveal you to the nations and the glory of your people Israel.” ✨
Joseph and Jesus’ mother were amazed at what people were saying about him.
Simeon blessed them and said to Mary, “This child is appointed to bring many in Israel down and raise many up. He’ll be a sign people speak against.”
“And a sword will pierce your own soul too, so the thoughts in many hearts can be revealed.”
There was also a prophet named Anna, daughter of Phanuel, from Asher’s tribe. She was very old: after marrying as a virgin, she had lived with her husband for seven years,
then had been a widow for about eighty-four years. She never left the temple, worshiping with fasting and prayer night and day.
Coming up at that very moment, Anna thanked the Lord and spoke about Jesus to everyone waiting for Jerusalem’s redemption.
When they had done everything required by the Lord’s Law, they returned to Galilee, to their own town of Nazareth.
The child grew and became strong, filled with wisdom. God’s grace rested on him. 🌱
Every year Jesus’ parents went to Jerusalem for the Passover festival.
When Jesus was twelve, they went up to Jerusalem for the festival, as they usually did.
When the festival days were over and they started home, the boy Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem. Joseph and his mother didn’t realize it.
They assumed he was somewhere in the traveling group and went a whole day before looking for him among their relatives and friends.
When they couldn’t find him, they went back to Jerusalem searching for him.
After three days, they found him in the temple, sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking questions.
Everyone who heard him was amazed at how much he understood and at his answers.
When his parents saw him, they were stunned. His mother said, “Son, why did you do this to us? Your father and I have been anxiously looking everywhere for you.”
He said to them, “Why were you looking for me? Didn’t you know I had to be in my Father’s house?”
They didn’t understand what he meant by that.
Jesus went back with them to Nazareth and was obedient to them. His mother kept all these things in her heart.
Jesus kept growing in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and people.
